correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, the unobserved line-graph vertices after the domination step are precisely the edges of K_U, U the isolated endpoints of the chosen edges. If |U|>=3, every observed vertex has 0 or |U|-1>=2 unobserved neighbors and no force is possible; if |U|=2, a single force suffices. This proves the exact iff criterion. Inclusion-exclusion over U yields the full polynomial. Removing an edge changes isolation by exactly the number of its degree-one endpoints, proving the exhaustive one-isolate matching and two-isolate star-forest classification. Matching/path enumeration and the labeled exponential formula yield all minimum and minimal-set coefficients; upper and lower extrema follow by counting covered vertices/components. Direct-definition finite enumeration for n=3,...,7 covered 2,131,016 masks, and independent exact polynomial arithmetic tested n=3,...,14. These computations do not substitute for the infinite proof.

evidence: Lu-Mao-Wang, arXiv:1808.02613v1, prove a bound for connected 4-regular claw-free graphs; J(n,2) has degree 2(n-2), so the theorem applies only at n=4.
Brimkov et al. 2018 give threshold-graph polynomials; J(n,2) contains an induced 4-cycle for n>=4 and hence is not threshold.
Power Domination Reconfiguration, DOI:10.1007/s44007-025-00187-5, discusses minimal-set/reconfiguration principles but its relevant Sections 3 and 5 do not classify L(K_n).

The later line-graph fault-tolerance paper (DOI:10.1038/s41598-026-54352-z) studies lifting PMU configurations and resilience, with no J(n,2) all-subset or all-minimal-set enumeration in its inspected pertinent results.

There remains a bounded risk of unindexed specialized equivalents.

value.rationale: Power monitoring on line graphs of complete networks is a natural graph-family problem, and the full placement distribution is a well-motivated refinement of a minimum parameter. The exact zero-or-one-step propagation boundary, complete all-set polynomial, exhaustive matching/star-forest inclusion-minimal family, closed minimum count, unbounded difference between upper and lower minimal cardinalities, and maximal-failure classification offer reusable structure for counting and robustness decisions. These statements require more than the generic definition, a preexisting finite table, or a lone textbook matching count. The result is intentionally restricted to J(n,2), not unsupported generalizations.
